question: Does equal-entity training weighting improve equal-new-entity prediction risk compared with equal-row training weighting in this fixed synthetic repeated-measurement problem?
target: uniformly sample a new entity, then uniformly sample one of its measurement rows
selection: For each objective mode choose learning rate by mean final equal-entity validation half-MSE over all three seeds; first listed rate breaks exact ties. No early stopping. Final deployment averages three predictions.
normalization: Both modes use the SAME training-only equal-entity feature mean and population standard deviation. No label standardization.
primary_contrast: entity ensemble minus row ensemble, paired equal-test-entity half-MSE

strong_baseline.features: all monomials of total degree <=3 including intercept
strong_baseline.selection: minimum equal-entity validation half-MSE, first listed lambda breaks exact ties
strong_baseline.solver: augmented weighted least squares; no matrix inverse

bootstrap.scope: conditional on fixed training data, model-selection decisions and fitted ensembles; no retraining or retuning

diagnostics.identity_leakage_note: Separate identity-only task, not a score for the main MLP problem; compare seen-entity held-out measurement and never-seen entity.

limits: Synthetic finite experiment; no universal benefit of entity weighting
MLP modes match candidates, seeds, architecture, updates and row presentations, not measured wall time
Classical baseline solver budgets are disclosed separately, not claimed equal to neural updates
Published test labels are for reproducibility, not a reusable blind leaderboard
